symptom: A retrieve constraint that spans lines or does not fit on one line stored the wrong string, under mdl 1 and mdl 0 alike: `'C:\temp'` stored a tab, and `'C:\'` ran into the rest of the constraint and stored `[Name = 'C:'' or\n Name = ']`. Under mdl 0 an access rule, a workflow targeting and a navigation sync constraint stored their strings as written (`'C:\\temp'` two backslashes, `'it\'s'` with an escape Mendix does not have), while a retrieve and a page datasource in the same script stored the value; describe of a page datasource, access rule, targeting, navigation constraint, dynamic query and retrieve limit/offset printed the stored text as it stands, so `'C:\temp'` re-read under mdl 0 as a tab.
cause: visitor.ParseXPathConstraint (and IsBracketedXPath) lexed a STORED constraint with the default mdl 0 lexer; FormatXPathConstraint re-derives the layout of every long or multi-line constraint from that parse on write, so the misread value was re-rendered into the model. The input is already Mendix spelling (the visitor transcribes it), so no script version was right for it. Separately bracketedXPathText and the navigation constraint kept the source verbatim, and each describer had its own string rule.
fix: ParseXPathConstraint and IsBracketedXPath read with parser.StrictEscapeStream (storedXPathStream): a stored constraint is always read the Mendix way. bracketedXPathText, the navigation constraint, the dynamic-query expression and retrieve limit/offset go through storedExpressionSource. Every describer goes through describeXPath / describeExprText (mdl0ExpressionStrings under mdl 0); ctx threaded through the page datasource and workflow formatters; quoted fallbacks use mdlQuote.
insight: The question for a re-parse is not 'which language is the script in' but 'whose spelling is this text in'. Text the visitor has already transcribed, or text read from the model, is Mendix spelling and must be read strictly whatever the header says; threading the script version into it would have fixed mdl 1 and left mdl 0 corrupting the same constraint. The previous finding's insight (enumerate a converter's call sites) found the other half: five describers and three write paths each had a private string rule.
